title: Why the lab cares about pancreas nerves
objective: Connect pancreatic innervation and interoception to metabolic control and the project.

steps.title: The nervous system watches metabolism
steps.body: Metabolism isn't only hormones. **[[interoception]]** — the nervous system's sense of the body's internal state — lets the brain monitor and influence organs like the pancreas. Sensory nerves to the pancreas may help the body track and tune glucose handling; that is still being worked out.

options: The nervous system's sense of the body's internal state
The ordinary sense of touch felt on the skin surface
The sense of body position and limb movement
The brain's autonomic control of the organs
steps.explanation: Interoception is the afferent sensing of internal organs — the input side of autonomic and metabolic control.

variants.setup: The brain tracks how full the stomach is and how fast the heart beats.
variants.reveal: Interoception is the body's sense of its own internal state.

steps.setup: You want to test whether sensory neurons innervating the pancreas influence glucose handling.
steps.prompt: Which approach fits the lab's project?
options: Silence those neurons with a DREADD and then measure glucose
Cut all nerves to the pancreas, then measure glucose
Feed the mice sugar and simply track their glucose
steps.reveal: Targeting pancreas afferents with a **[[DREADD]]** and watching glucose/physiology is exactly your capstone project — extending the colon playbook to a metabolic organ.

variants.prompt: To test if pancreas sensory neurons affect metabolism, the lab would…
options: Silence them with a DREADD and read out glucose
Cut all nerves to the pancreas, then read glucose
Feed the mice sugar and track their glucose
variants.explanation: DREADD silencing with a metabolic readout isolates the neurons' role.

steps.title: Where the tracks meet
steps.body: D7 (metabolism) + the sensory biology (Track A) + the tools (Track C) converge on the capstone: do pancreas-innervating sensory neurons shape glucose control? That's a frontier question — the pancreas isn't yet mapped the way the colon is.

flag.note: Sensory control of pancreatic/metabolic function is an active, unsettled research area.

sources.note: Spinal sensory innervation of the intestine; interoceptive control of visceral organs.
